name: Belief-Substrate Divinity
laws: Gods exist because they are believed in
Forgotten gods diminish; unbelieved gods die or change
New gods rise from new kinds of attention (media, internet, highway)
costs: Gods must work to maintain belief — con, blood, ritual
Assimilation to a new culture changes the god
limits: Cannot fully escape the form belief gave them
Old World gods in America are always immigrants
examples: American Gods — the full pantheon logic
Sandman — Morpheus's dependence on the Dreaming's imagination

name: Dreaming as Territory
laws: Morpheus rules; his rule is mostly observation
Waking breaches the Dreaming at the edges
costs: A dream without a dreamer is a risk
Morpheus binds stories that escape their tellers
Those who trespass in the Dreaming risk being rewritten
limits: Cannot override a dreamer's autonomous imagination
Cannot prevent nightmares that are owed
examples: Preludes & Nocturnes — Morpheus reclaiming the Dreaming
